title: Oct 15 Results + Oct 16 Preview: Split the Slate, Ready to Bounce Back
summary: Went 1-1 on Oct 15. Tomorrow we're backing the Rays with Martinez on the bump.

content.value:
## Oct 15 Recap: A Pitcher's Take

Went .500 yesterday with a 1-1 record. Not what we're aiming for, but that's baseball. Hit on the Guardians pick at home—when you're backing the home team with a 52% edge, you take those wins. The Dodgers miss at 61% confidence stings a bit more. From a pitcher's perspective, October baseball is unpredictable. One mistake pitch changes everything.

## What Went Right and Wrong

The **Guardians** came through at home. That's the advantage you want in October—pitching depth and home field. We read that one correctly.

The **Dodgers** miss? That's postseason variance. At 61% confidence, we felt good about LA, but the Brewers had other plans. Sometimes the underdog's starter just finds another gear. I've been on both sides of that as a pitcher—you either dominate or get shelled, rarely in between during playoff baseball.

## Oct 16 Preview: Rays @ Guardians Rematch

Tomorrow we're flipping the script. After backing Cleveland yesterday, the model likes **Tampa Bay at 54%** in the rematch. It's essentially a coin flip, but there's an edge here.

**Nick Martinez** takes the ball for the Rays against **Shawn Armstrong** for Cleveland. From a pitcher's perspective, Martinez has been solid—he knows how to work hitters and keep the ball on the ground. Armstrong coming out of the pen as an opener or bulk guy changes the dynamics entirely.

## The Pitching Matchup Breakdown

Martinez is a veteran who understands October baseball. He's not going to overpower you, but he'll locate, change speeds, and keep your offense off-balance. That's exactly what you need in a playoff environment.

Armstrong on the other side is a different animal—likely working in a shorter stint. Cleveland might be bullpenning this one, which can work but also creates more variables. More pitchers means more chances for one guy to not have his best stuff.

I'm trusting Martinez to give Tampa length and keep it close. The Rays have the pitching infrastructure to steal one on the road.

## Bottom Line

Oct 15 was a push—frustrating but manageable. We move forward. Oct 16 brings a tight matchup where pitching depth and execution will decide it. I like Tampa Bay's chances with Martinez on the mound. It's not a high-confidence slam dunk, but 54% with the right pitcher in a playoff setting? I'll take that edge.

Let's get back to winning baseball tomorrow.
